node.label: Anthony Giddens
node.date_label: The Constitution of Society (1984) · The Consequences of Modernity (1990) · Modernity and Self-Identity (1991)
node.description: Develops structuration as an account of how social practices reproduce and transform the rules and resources on which they depend. Structure is both enabling and constraining, not merely an outside force confronting a free individual. The selected chapter also makes time and space constitutive of social practice: purposeful conduct unfolds through embodied, situated activity, and its consequences exceed what actors intend. This avoids treating either an individual subject or a social whole as a self-sufficient starting point. The earlier Sewell abstract identifies a later reformulation, while its limited reading does not establish every detail of that criticism.
